subject: Low-latency pathing qualification & pilot plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Matthew Cho <matthew.cho@streamlineai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-18T09:02:00Z
Subject: Low-latency pathing qualification & pilot plan

Matt — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Major ask: validate that these match what you expect and flag anything we missed.

Key SLO goals you stated on the call:
- p50 generation RTT: <= 60ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens)
- p95 generation RTT: <= 220ms
- sustained throughput: 120 requests/sec (avg request ~40 tokens)
- concurrency burst target: 200 concurrent sessions (streaming enabled)
- streaming note: token-by-token delivery with first-byte latency <= 50ms after request accepted

Primary risk areas we identified:
- prefix / context cache hit-rate (you said 60% of requests reuse the same conversation prefixes)
- model size tradeoffs — accuracy vs decode latency
- quantization impact on streaming jitter

Cost / performance levers we recommend evaluating in the pilot:
1) Continuous batching: target per-GPU batch window = 10ms for low-latency mode; measure p50/p95 delta vs single-request path.
2) Prefix KV caching: populate warmed KV cache for high-reuse users during canary to reduce compute per request.
3) Model variants: pilot with two variants — Redwood-compact-3B (fast, ~10% lower quality) and Redwood-base-7B (baseline). Use A/B routing by user cohort.
4) Quantization profiles: 8-bit dynamic first, then 4-bit QAT if quality holds. Track hallucination/regression with eval set.
5) Graceful fallback: if p95 exceeds target, route to a cheaper non-streaming variant while preserving first-byte SLA.

Proposed minimal pilot scope (2 weeks):
- Week 0: exchange workload profile (I've attached a CSV template).
- Week 1: Redwood runs pilot in hosted dedicated capacity with two model variants and KV cache warmed for the top 10 conversation prefixes.
- Week 2: Collect telemetry (latency histograms by model/route, cache hit rates, token cost), run quality regression against the provided eval set.

Action items / owners:
- Matthew: confirm workload CSV and provide sample traffic replay or recorded trace by Friday (03/22).
- Aditya: will own pilot infra and routing config.
- Grace: will run cost estimates and prepare a short SLA note for the pilot.
- Vivek: coordinate and produce the pilot runbook.

Attachments: streamline-workload-profile.csv (workload template), slo-eval-template.xlsx (quality + latency checks).

If this looks right, we can lock pilot dates and schedule a short kickoff (30 min) with your infra/ops next week.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Matthew Cho <matthew.cho@streamlineai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@streamlineai.com
Date: 2028-03-18T12:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Low-latency pathing qualification & pilot plan

Thanks Vivek — solid summary. A few clarifications from our side: we can produce a traffic replay but two notes:
1) The 120 req/sec is an average across our edge; peak short bursts hit ~300 req/sec for a minute or two during user onboarding flows.
2) Streaming is our priority for chat UX — we need first-token as fast as possible; tradeoffs on quality are acceptable if we preserve p50 first-byte < 60ms.

Questions:
- For continuous batching, does Redwood give us a control knob for target batch window per route? We want tighter windows for onboarding users.
- On model variants: can we get explicit latency estimates per variant (cold vs warmed KV cache) so we can reason about routing?
- For quantization: worried about degredation on named-entity extraction in our domain. Can you include a short A/B test for NER precision?

We'll try to get you a replay and an internal ops contact for onboarding (ops-team@streamlineai.com). ETA for the replay: COB Thursday (03/22).

—Matt
Matthew Cho
VP Product — StreamlineAI
matthew.cho@streamlineai.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Matthew Cho <matthew.cho@streamlineai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-18T13:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Low-latency pathing qualification & pilot plan

Matt — great notes. Short answers + what we'll deliver in the pilot: 

- Batch window knob: yes — Redwood Dedicated exposes per-route target_batch_window_ms (we'll start at 10ms for low-latency route and 50ms for throughput-optimized route). We'll capture tradeoffs in the telemetry dashboard.
- Variant latency estimates: Aditya will produce p50/p95 estimates for compact-3B and base-7B in both cold (no KV) and warmed KV cache states. Expect ~20-40ms delta p50 between compact-3B and base-7B on A100-like hardware; warmed KV cache can reduce decode time by ~25% for prefix-heavy requests. We'll provide the numbers before pilot start.
- NER regression: we'll run the provided NER eval set as part of the quality checks. If quantization causes >2% F1 drop, we will not promote that quantized variant for streaming.

Pilot deliverables list (concrete):
1) Telemetry dashboard with latency histograms by route/model and cache-hit tag.
2) Cost report: tokens consumed, GPU-hours, and estimated per-request unit cost for each configuration.
3) Regression matrix: NER F1, BLEU-like assist metrics, and hallucination rate for each model/quant profile.
4) Routing plan: simple rule set to map users to variants by cohort, with automatic fallback thresholds.

Aditya — can you take point on the latency estimates and attach a short table to the kickoff agenda? Grace — can you run an initial cost estimate based on typical week-of-traffic (Aditya will share model sizes)?

If Matthew's ops team sends the replay by Thu COB we'll aim to start the canary the week of Mar 27. Kickoff invite proposed for Thu 03/22 16:00 PT — I'll share a calendar invite once Matthew confirms.

Vivek
